candidate.title: Organizer add-guests email sets Reply-To to all attendee emails, leaking roster and risking oversized headers
reports: packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:25 — replyto includes every attendee email, leaking the full attendee list to each team member recipient.
team-member variant of organizer email sends mismatched organizer-personalized content without teammember prop, and replyto includes all attendees leaking emails

[advisory] replyto is built as the organizer plus every attendee email with no bound, and the attendee list grows with every add-guests call. on seats bookings or after repeated guest additions the header accumulates dozens of addresses until strict smtp receivers reject the organizer's notification outright; it also discloses every attendee address to each recipient, defeating seatsshowattendees=false.

[advisory] replyto is built by appending the organizer email plus every attendee email with no bound, so the header grows linearly with attendee count. on bookings with many attendees (large seat-based bookings, or after repeated addguests calls), the reply-to header exceeds smtp recipient header limits and the receiving server rejects or truncates the message, silently failing delivery of the organizer notification.

[bug] organizeraddguestsemail builds the reply-to header by appending every attendee email with no bound — replyto: [this.calevent.organizer.email, ...this.calevent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)] — so the header grows linearly with attendee count. once a booking accumulates many guests (this feature permits unbounded adds), the oversized reply-to header exceeds smtp/header size limits and the organizer notification email fails to send.

[advisory] the replyto header is built by appending every attendee email (organizer plus all attendees) with no bound, and this list grows cumulatively every time guests are added to the booking. repeated use of the add-guests feature on a popular booking grows the organizer notification's replyto header without limit until the sending mail provider rejects it — at which point the failure is swallowed by the handler's catch (console.log only), so attendees silently stop receiving any notifications.
